stable.label: iOS 27.0.1
stable.notes: Bug-fix-only release addressing Wi-Fi disconnects, Bluetooth pairing failures (AirPods/CarPlay), and Face ID false rejections reported after the iOS 27.0 launch on Sept 14–18, 2026. No new features.

upcomingFeature.label: iOS 27.1
upcomingFeature.notes: Estimated feature update — expected to add Apple Intelligence Custom Voice (general availability), additional Apple Cash features, RCS business messaging, and the Siri EU language rollout. Date is a community estimate, not confirmed by Apple — check Settings for the actual release.

beta.label: iOS 27.2 (beta)
beta.notes: Early developer beta, already in testing for the release after 27.1. Contains App Tracking Transparency changes for EU users and minor StoreKit fixes. Not recommended on a primary device.

communitySentiment.label: Mostly stable after 27.0.1
communitySentiment.summary: iOS 27.0 launch-day reports included Wi-Fi drops, Bluetooth pairing failures, and Face ID false rejections on newer Pro models. Apple's 27.0.1 bug-fix patch, released within days, addressed those three issues, and no major new problems have been reported against it since. A temporary battery dip for 24–48 hours after any update is normal while the system reindexes Spotlight and Photos — it is not itself a sign of a bad update.
communitySentiment.sourceNote: Compiled by hand from public beta-tester and release-note reporting (MacRumors forums, Apple's own release notes, tech press). Not a live feed — refresh this file's data manually after checking current reports, or wire in a real backend if you want continuous monitoring.

pointReleaseAdvice: Point releases (x.0.1, x.1) bring bug and security fixes with low risk — install those as they appear. The first .0 release of a major version carries the most risk; if you're not in a hurry, waiting for the first bug-fix patch (as happened here with 27.0.1) is a reasonable way to skip the roughest week.
